page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-192-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine tailored for data-intensive enterprise workloads requiring vast memory capacity and direct local flash storage. Operating on the x86_64 processor architecture, the instance provides 192 dedicated vCPUs paired with 1512 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation ratio of 7.88 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not included in this configuration.

A central component of this instance is its high-density local storage array. The server bundles 24 local NVMe SSD drives supplying an aggregate capacity of 90,194 GB. This direct-attached NVMe storage structure bypasses network-attached block storage latencies, enabling sustained high-throughput and low-latency input/output operations. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provisioned with this machine type.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance consolidates 192 dedicated cores, over 1.5 TB of RAM, and more than 90 TB of high-speed local disk onto a single node. This hardware profile provides high compute and storage density, eliminating the network fabric bottlenecks and operational complexity associated with multi-node cluster architectures.

The hardware configuration is suitable for large-scale relational databases, distributed NoSQL data stores, extensive in-memory caching solutions, and high-throughput extract, transform, load (ETL) processing workloads.

This resource profile makes the instance appropriate for enterprise transactional databases, distributed NoSQL systems, in-memory caching platforms, and data warehousing pipelines requiring substantial local storage throughput.
